metas.name: Grave of the Fireflies
metas.description: Captures war as two children slowly running out of everything. A brother tries to keep his little sister fed and cheerful in Kobe, 1945, making worse decisions out of pride.

metas.name: Perfect Blue
metas.description: Captures fame eating a person's grip on which self is hers. A pop idol turned actress, a stalker, and a fan site narrating her life in first person — the animated form is what makes the slippage work.

metas.name: Waltz with Bashir
metas.description: Captures a soldier's memory with a hole in it. Animated interviews as the director tries to recover what he did in Beirut in 1982, ending with footage that breaks the animation open.

metas.name: Flee
metas.description: Captures telling a hidden life story for the first time. An animated documentary about a refugee from Afghanistan settled in Denmark, recounting flight, family separation and a secret he has kept from everyone.

metas.name: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
metas.director: Bob Persichetti, Peter Ramsey, Rodney Rothman
metas.description: Captures what a comic book actually feels like to read, in motion. Also a genuinely good story about a kid learning that anyone can wear the mask, by failing at it a lot.

metas.name: Princess Mononoke
metas.description: Captures an ecological war with no pure side. Iron Town needs the forest cut to survive; the forest gods need the humans gone; a prince cursed by a dying god tries to see with unclouded eyes.

metas.name: Paddington 2
metas.description: Captures decency as something contagious. A bear framed for stealing the pop-up book he wanted to buy his aunt, sent to prison — and the prison improves because he is in it.

metas.name: Paprika
metas.description: Captures dreams invading waking life as a parade. A device that lets therapists enter dreams is stolen, and reality dissolves into a marching band of refrigerators and dolls; Inception's debt is on screen.

metas.name: It's Such a Beautiful Day
metas.description: Captures a mind coming apart, drawn with stick figures. Hertzfeldt narrates a man with a failing brain in three chapters — funny, fragmented, and by the end genuinely cosmic.

metas.name: The Tale of the Princess Kaguya
metas.description: Captures joy being disciplined out of a girl. A bamboo cutter raises a moon princess and watches court life sand down the wild child she was, until the watercolour lines themselves start to run.

metas.name: Wolfwalkers
metas.description: Captures the wild being hunted in the name of order. Kilkenny, 1650: a hunter's daughter befriends a girl who becomes a wolf in her sleep, and Cartoon Saloon's hand-drawn forest keeps breaking out of the town's straight lines.

metas.name: Tower
metas.description: Captures how people inside an event remember it — partial, sensory, nothing like the news summary. The 1966 UT Austin sniper massacre retold in rotoscoped animation from survivors' memories, switching to real footage only at the end.

metas.name: Tale of Tales
metas.description: Captures folk memory itself — images from childhood, war and lullaby sharing one continuous dream. Norstein's 29-minute animation drifts through layers of cut-out, glass and mist: a little wolf, a minotaur, tango dancers, soldiers leaving for the front.

metas.name: Alice
metas.description: Captures the folk tale as a child's-eye inventory of a household's dangerous things. Švankmajer's Alice moves through a Wonderland of taxidermy, bones and jam jars of pins, stop-motion objects that genuinely threaten her — Carroll's dream rebuilt from junk drawers.
